cohort: The study included adolescents aged 13-17 years (52% girls) who were born either very preterm with FGR (n=24), very preterm with appropriate birth weight (n=27), or at term with appropriate birth weight (n=28).
finding: Very preterm birth due to fetal growth restriction was associated with higher, yet normal, daytime and 24-hour mean arterial blood pressures in adolescent boys compared to term AGA boys, with male sex and FGR enhancing this effect, while no group differences were observed in girls or arterial stiffness.
birth_weight: Appropriate birth weight (AGA) for two control groups; fetal growth restriction (FGR) for the primary study group.
gest_age: Very preterm birth and at term birth
